## Creating, configuring and publishing an OpenLayers webmap

*This tutorial has been created for learning purposes.*

Welcome to the OpenLayers webmapping tutorial! In this tutorial, you will build an interactive webmap using OpenLayers, an open-source JavaScript library for displaying geospatial data in a web browser.

You will start with a basic map and gradually develop it by adding geospatial data, adjusting the map view, styling layers and building interface elements. By the end, you will have a working webmap that you can publish online.

You do not need to be an experienced programmer to complete the exercises. However, you should be comfortable working with files and folders, and be prepared to edit some HTML, CSS and JavaScript code.


## Learning objectives
After completing this tutorial, you have learned:
- How to initiate an OpenLayers file structure, and how to edit the key files for creating an interactive webmap. 
- Where to find resources for adding UI elements to your webmap, and how to modify them to be suitable for your project.
- How to bring data layers from various data sources to your webmap, and attribute them accordingly. 
- How to utilise GitHub pages for serving your OpenLayers webmap to the world. 


## Structure
This tutorial has been divided into thematic sections, each bringing a new element to your webmap. 

- 01 Setup - Installing needed software for initiating an OpenLayers webmap file structure
- 02 WMS layer - Add a WebMapService layer
- 03 Map view - Edit the map window
- 04 GeoJSON layers - Add local GeoJSON layers
- 05 Vector styles - Edit GeoJSON layer styles
- 06 Basemap switcher - Switch between two basemap options
- 07 Legend - Create legend that match layer styles
- 08 Title - Edit map title
- 09 Info panel - Add a toggled abstract
- 10 Publish - Publish the finished webmap on GitHub Pages
